justification: The lot reader that proves a single-site outline against the NSW cadastre silently dropped any lot written with a section ("Lot 3 Sec D DP 119"), because its pattern needed "Lot N, DP" with nothing between. A site could then be built, or fail, on fewer lots than the council names. Leichhardt Part G (G6, G7, G9, G10) writes lots this way, and G7 and G12 use "67 to 78" and en-dash ranges. This change teaches parse_lots those forms. It changes no database row and loads no outline.

falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the fix, on this branch, the six new tests failed: 6 failed / 7 passed. test_section_letter_is_part_of_the_lot_id failed with 'At index 0 diff: 2//DP234045 != 3/D/DP119', which is the section lot being dropped without a message.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: parse_lots stops reading a section, a 'to' range or an en-dash range. Measured on this branch: with the old parse_lots and the six new tests, 6 failed / 7 passed (the first failure shows 'Lot 3 Sec D DP 119' dropped: index 0 was '2//DP234045', not '3/D/DP119'). With the new parse_lots, 13 passed. Related tests (-k site_boundar or site_figure or site_address): 28 passed.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The NSW cadastre table nsw_cadastre_lots decides what a lot id looks like. Read on 2026-11-04: lots with a section are stored as lot/section/DPnnn ('3/D/DP119', '3/1/DP328'), lots without one as lot//DPnnn ('59//DP4844'). The tests take their wording from the council's own Leichhardt Part G PDF pages 31, 65, 105, 116 and 139, not from the reader's output.

pre_impl.existing_data: scripts/build_site_boundaries.py already holds the lot reader, the five proof checks and the load step; tests/test_build_site_boundaries.py already tests ranges and 'and' lists. Nothing parallel was built. The cadastre id format was read from nsw_cadastre_lots (columns lotnumber, sectionnumber, plannumber exist).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Existing: the lot reader, the five proof checks and the load step in scripts/build_site_boundaries.py, reused unchanged. New: only the lot pattern and the id it builds, so a section, a 'to' range and an en or em dash range are read. No new script, table or file was added.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I assumed the eight Leichhardt site lists (G6 to G13) could be dry-run with the existing reader. They could not: four use a section word, G7 uses 'to', G12 an en dash. A dry run of G11 and G8 earlier the same day showed the proof checks work but could not cover the other six, which is what this change fixes.

functions.name: parse_lots
functions.input: the lot sentence copied from a chapter page, e.g. 'Lot 3 Sec D DP 119 , Lot 2 DP 234045'
functions.output: a de-duplicated list of cadastre lot ids, 'lot/section/DPnnn', section empty when none is written
functions.if_none: text with no 'Lot ... DP nnn' returns an empty list; the caller (prove) then fails check 2_lots because the lot list is empty, so a site is never built from nothing

break_it.scenario: A section word leaks onto the next lot, so 'Lot 25 Sec 1 DP 328, Lot A DP 377714' returns A/1/DP377714.
break_it.what_happens: The lot would not be found in the cadastre, and check 2_lots would refuse to build the site. It cannot pass silently.

break_it.scenario: The section is written in lower case or the same lot is named twice, so the id differs from the cadastre's or appears twice.
break_it.what_happens: A lower-case section would give an id the cadastre does not hold and check 2_lots would refuse the site; a duplicate would be counted twice in lots_listed.
break_it.how: Measured on 2026-11-04: 'Lot 3 sec d DP 119' returns ['3/D/DP119'], and the same lot named twice returns it once.
break_it.repro: python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import build_site_boundaries as b;print(b.parse_lots('Lot 3 sec d DP 119'))"

break_it.scenario: The word 'to' inside ordinary prose is read as a range, for example 'Lot 2 to the north DP 5'.
break_it.what_happens: A range needs an id on both sides of 'to'. Measured: parse_lots('Lot 2 to the north DP 5') returns [] (no lot is read at all, and check 2_lots then refuses the site), and 'Lot 2 to 4 DP 5' returns lots 2, 3 and 4.
break_it.how: Measured on 2026-11-04 with the two strings above; the 11 existing sites all parse identically to before.

mutation_analysis: One mutation, run rather than described: the old parse_lots against the new tests gives 6 failed / 7 passed, so each of the six new tests fails when the behaviour is missing. I did not run a second mutation that breaks only the range separator, so a defect in 'to' alone relies on test_to_makes_a_range_and_is_not_a_lot, which asserts 13 lots with exact first, second and last ids.
residual_risk: The reader still depends on the sentence being copied verbatim from the page; a lot written in a form not covered (measured: 'Lot 4, Section 2, DP 99' reads as 4/2/DP99, but 'Lot 4 in DP 99 Sec 2' returns []) would be dropped without a message, as before. No Leichhardt outline is loaded by this change; G8's lot 1 DP 632522 is not in the cadastre and G7's lots 67 to 78 appear missing, so those sites still need another source.
